decision.root_cause: Requiring a registration to contain its own final squash SHA or a subsequently created repair issue ID creates a circular bootstrap. Protected registration should identify PR relationships known before merge; verified GitHub execution supplies the resulting commit and publication IDs afterward.
evidence: Current read-only inspection found a clean worktree at 87a2b75855e818823bdfcebf339bc5c14aa37982, with the earlier arbitration recorded and no W11-010 lineage registration present.
The controller can register a real PR number before queue enrollment; its final merged SHA and any failure-created repair issue number are unavailable at that stage.

GitHub supports ordinary comments on PRs through the Issues API using issues:write, so a separate tracker issue is unnecessary. [Issue comments](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/comments#create-an-issue-comment)

GitHub provides commit-to-PR association for verifying the PR introducing the source run's commit. [Commit association](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/commits#list-pull-requests-associated-with-a-commit)
directed_repair: Place registration under each existing tickets[] entry as post_merge_registration: {version: 1, attempts: [...]}. Each attempt has exactly pr_number, predecessor_pr_number, and repair_issue_number. The originating attempt has null predecessors and null repair_issue_number. A repair attempt references its immediate predecessor PR and the already-existing repair issue. Inherit ticket_id from the containing ticket; derive the stable lineage key from repository identity, ticket ID, and the first registered PR number.

Do not require originating_commit, protected_commits, tracker_issue_number, originating_pr_number, predecessor_lineage_id, or a future repair_issue_id in registration. The first attempt already identifies the originating PR. Keep source_workflow_path and required_jobs in the existing shared workflow/quality contract, not per-attempt metadata. Simulation namespace belongs exclusively to the isolated simulation configuration.

After creating the real PR, the controller commits its registration on that PR branch before queue enrollment. Re-run checks on the resulting head. Registration becomes trusted when that PR reaches protected develop. Do not register invented PR numbers, placeholder SHAs, or a commit's own hash.

For the first post-merge run, read the manifest at the verified source run's head_sha. Find the uniquely registered PR that GitHub confirms is merged into develop with merge_commit_sha equal to head_sha. Derive the final merged SHA from this agreement between the trusted run and GitHub PR data. No pre-existing manifest completion_evidence or protected_commits entry is required. Missing derived output fields must not block an otherwise valid initial run.

Use the verified source PR number as the PASS/evidence projection target. Create or update a dedicated publisher comment through /issues/{pr_number}/comments; preserve the PR body and merged state. Include the exact source SHA, run/attempt, workflow, suite/provider and conclusions. Treat the comment as a projection; only the controller records authoritative manifest completion.

On the first verified failure, discover or create the deduplicated repair issue using the previously directed provenance checks and serialized reconciliation. Its number is a runtime output, not a prerequisite for processing that failure. A later protected registration is not required to recognize a rerun: validate the existing candidate against the registered originating PR and genuine failure run. Ambiguous candidates still fail closed.

When a repair PR later exists, the controller appends its attempt entry in that repair PR, using the already-known predecessor PR and repair issue number. Preserve previous entries. Derive every attempt's merged SHA through GitHub verification and validate predecessor ancestry. Repair issue registration therefore occurs in a future repair PR, never through a special direct push or a bookkeeping-only prerequisite for the initial finalizer.

For stale-result protection, reconcile registrations from a captured protected develop tip as well as the source commit. Determine the latest merged registered attempt through verified PR data and ancestry; an older source result remains historical and cannot close a later repair. Do not equate an unrelated newer develop commit with a new attempt in this lineage.

Add tests proving an initial registration with no commit hashes and no repair issue number successfully publishes PASS; first FAIL creates one repair issue; rerun reuses it before any registration update; and a later registered repair supersedes an older PASS. Retain all previously required completion and live simulation evidence.
manifest_changes: Document the optional post_merge_registration.version=1 and attempts schema within the existing manifest contract. No actual PR registration is authorized or performed by this read-only response.

Require real registration before queue enrollment, not before PR creation. Validate positive unique PR numbers, a single originating attempt, and an unambiguous predecessor chain; repair attempts require an existing repair issue number.

Keep derived merged SHAs, run IDs, suite/provider evidence, comment IDs and newly created repair issue IDs in runtime evidence and subsequent controller bookkeeping, outside required bootstrap inputs.
Preserve manifest schema_version 6 unless existing schema validation requires an explicit compatibility bump; do not introduce a second top-level schema_version for lineage records.
Preserve zero retries, existing permissions, completion requirements, dependency DAG, and deferred live OBS authorization.
